chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not create for people absolute freedom in their actions, but He gave them choice and free will.

key_terms.حُرِّيَّةٌ: Freedom/Liberty (in the context of unrestricted action)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on free will and determinism in human actions?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq articulates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters), rejecting both absolute determinism (*jabr*) and total unrestricted freedom (*tafwid*). This nuanced position establishes that while human agency is real and necessary for moral accountability, it operates within the broader divine will, thereby grounding the justice of divine recompense in a balanced metaphysical framework.
